_about: What the GDD (docs/game_bible.md) requires of the game code, one entry per feature, for tools/feature-agent/feature_agent.mjs. 'detect' rules are checked against game/ (paths relative to it): a requirement is met when all its rules pass. 'status' is the bible item's status (Locked weighs more than Proposed). 'impact' and 'effort' are 1-5. 'depends' lists requirement ids that must be met first.

requirements.title: Core loop scenes
requirements.bible: Game identity > Core loop: read chat, inspect search results and reviews, recommend, see the reaction.

requirements.title: Static JSON content, no runtime AI or network calls
requirements.bible: Game identity > Engine: Phaser 3, static JSON loaded at startup, no runtime AI calls.

requirements.title: Scoring: hard check, start at 3, -1 per soft miss, floor of 1
requirements.bible: Scoring rules (Locked).

requirements.title: Portrait per emotion tag, unknown tags fall back to NEUTRAL
requirements.bible: Emotion tags and art rules: any unknown tag falls back to NEUTRAL; portrait_<character>_<tag>.

requirements.title: One icon per cuisine
requirements.bible: Emotion tags and art rules > Venue icon: one per cuisine, icon_<cuisine>.png.

requirements.title: Notebook sidebar fed by tagged lines
requirements.bible: Data schemas > Dialogue: tagged lines feed the Notebook sidebar as the player reads them.

requirements.title: Partial-success hint names each miss; reread highlights the missed line
requirements.bible: Scoring rules > Partial success: hint names each missed preference. Data schemas: a partial-success hint highlights the tagged line the player missed.

requirements.title: Failed level must be retried
requirements.bible: Scoring rules > Complete failure: 0 stars, Failed, retry with a hint.

requirements.title: Scrapbook pages unlocked by callbacks
requirements.bible: Campaign structure > Scrapbook (Locked): a page unlocks the first time the player reads a line tagged with its id.

requirements.title: Credits file generated from the music folder
requirements.bible: Game identity > Audio (Locked): free or copyright-free lo-fi tracks, sourced by hand from Bensound and Pixabay Music, not by agents. Each track's license and any required credit are logged in a credits file shown in the game's credits screen.
requirements.spec: Fill game/public/credits.json's "music" list with every audio file in assets/music/ at the repo root (mp3 or ogg; the sync step copies them to game/public/music/, where the game serves them), all downloaded by Gabriella from Pixabay Music. Some have a Pixabay license certificate (*-license.txt in assets/music/, starting 'PIXABAY LICENSE CERTIFICATE'); match a track to its certificate by the Pixabay ID number in both file names (e.g. lafrey_music-art-aesthetic-599374.mp3 and beats-art-aesthetic-599374-license.txt). For a track WITH a certificate, take title (Audio File Title), artist (the username in the Licensor's Username URL), url (Audio File URL) and license_file ("music/<certificate name>") from it. For a track WITHOUT one (Gabriella confirmed these are free under Pixabay's license too), derive title and artist from the file name as well as possible (Pixabay names files <username>-<title words>-<id>.mp3), set url and license_file to null, and add "check": true so Gabriella can confirm the names. Every entry: file ("music/<file name>"), title, artist, source "Pixabay Music", license "Pixabay Content License", url, license_file, credit_line "<title> by <artist> (Pixabay)". Never choose, download, rename or delete music files. Keep the existing "art" entry. BootScene keeps loading credits.json into the registry as 'credits'.

requirements.title: Credits screen
requirements.bible: Game identity > Audio (Locked): ... logged in a credits file shown in the game's credits screen.
requirements.spec: Add src/scenes/CreditsScene.js (scene key 'Credits'), registered in main.js, reached from a 'Credits' button on the menu and back with '← Levels' and Esc. It lists every entry of the registry's 'credits' (music: title, artist, source, license and credit_line; art). With no music yet it says so plainly. Long lists scroll (ui/scroll.js). Use the theme's text()/pixel()/readText() and C colours; respect the game's accessibility rules in CLAUDE.md.

requirements.title: Background music from the credited tracks
requirements.bible: Game identity > Audio (Locked): free or copyright-free lo-fi tracks.
requirements.spec: Add src/ui/music.js: plays only tracks listed in the registry's 'credits'.music (files under public/music/, paths as given in each entry's "file"), looping through them at a low volume, starting only after the player's first click or key press (browsers block autoplay). If the list is empty it does nothing and never errors. Exports start(scene), setEnabled(on) and isEnabled(). Loading the audio files is done in BootScene from the credits list.

requirements.title: Music on/off in Options
requirements.bible: Game identity > Audio (Locked); the game's accessibility options live on the Options screen.
requirements.spec: Add a 'music' setting (On / Off, default On) to src/ui/settings.js OPTIONS and a row for it on the Options screen; apply it through music.js setEnabled().

requirements.title: Chapter intro cards
requirements.bible: Campaign structure > Calendar: each chapter is a season. 1 Campus Quarter, Spring semester: between classes, study groups. 2 Downtown, Summer internships: lunch breaks. 3 Night Market, Late summer nights: warm evenings. 4 Waterfront, End of summer: before Maya's trip, quiet dinners and celebrations.
requirements.spec: Add src/ui/chapterIntro.js exporting showChapterIntro(scene, chapter, onDone): a card over the screen with 'CHAPTER N', the district name and the season, plus one line from the bible's Calendar 'typical reasons' (use only the Calendar wording above, no new story text). It appears the first time a level of a new chapter opens (before its chat starts) and never again automatically (remember it in localStorage, wrapped in try/catch); tapping a chapter heading on the menu shows it again. Continue with a click, Enter or Esc. Animate only through tween() from src/ui/motion.js; use C colours and the theme text helpers.

requirements.title: How to play, before level 1
requirements.bible: Game identity > Core loop: read chat, inspect search results and reviews, recommend, see the reaction.
requirements.spec: Add src/ui/howToPlay.js exporting showHowToPlay(scene, onDone): a three-step overlay (1. read the group chat and notice what each friend needs; 2. open each place and read its reviews; 3. recommend the one place that suits everyone), each step pointing at the part of the screen it means. Shown automatically the first time level 1 opens (remember in localStorage, wrapped in try/catch), skippable at any step, keyboard-operable (Enter next, Esc skip). The Options screen gets a 'How to play' button that shows it again. Animate only through tween().

requirements.title: Star totals and progress
requirements.bible: Scoring rules: every level scores 0-3 stars. Campaign structure: 4 chapters of 5 levels.
requirements.spec: Add src/logic/progress.js (pure, no Phaser) exporting starTotals(levels, progress) -> { byChapter: { <chapter>: { earned, max } }, earned, max }, counting only built levels (max = 3 per level) and each level's best stars. The menu shows each chapter heading with 'earned / max' stars and a campaign total, and a small 'perfect' mark on a chapter where every built level has 3 stars. Add a check of starTotals to test/boot-test.mjs.

requirements.title: Keyboard play everywhere
requirements.bible: Game identity > Tone: cozy and welcoming. The game already has accessibility options on its Options screen.
requirements.spec: Make a whole level playable without a mouse. Restaurant list: up/down moves a visible focus ring between venue cards, Enter selects, and Enter again (or R) recommends. Outcome screen: left/right moves between its buttons, Enter presses. Scrapbook: left/right turns between unlocked pages (an open book since 2026-11-23, Gabriella). Menu: arrow keys move between level cards, Enter opens. Focus rings use C.highlight and stay visible in high contrast. The Chat and Options screens already support the keyboard; keep them as they are.

requirements.title: Reset progress
requirements.bible: Game identity > Structure: levels unlock in order as each is cleared.
requirements.spec: Add resetProgress() to src/ui/widgets.js that clears saved stars ('lets-eat-progress-v1'), Scrapbook pages ('lets-eat-scrapbook-v1') and 'been here' history ('lets-eat-venues-v1') from localStorage (wrapped in try/catch) and keeps the accessibility settings. The Options screen gets a 'Reset progress' button with a confirmation step drawn in the game (no browser confirm()): 'Reset' clears and returns to the menu, 'Cancel' changes nothing.

requirements.title: City map menu
requirements.bible: Campaign structure: each chapter unlocks a new neighbourhood of one fictional city (Campus Quarter, Downtown, Night Market, Waterfront).
requirements.spec: Add src/ui/cityMap.js exporting cityMap(scene, opts): the four districts drawn as a simple placeholder map (shapes in each district's own colour, labels with the district name and its star total from starTotals) until real art exists under the texture key 'city_map', which it uses when loaded. Districts whose chapter has no unlocked level look locked (greyed, no click). Clicking an unlocked district shows its level cards as the menu does today. The menu uses cityMap() instead of the plain chapter rows. Keep the Options and Scrapbook buttons.

requirements.title: Friends page
requirements.bible: Cast: each friend has permanent traits (allergies, strict diets, baseline budget, personality, voice). Clue rules: every scoring constraint appears in the chat; implied clues are never said outright.
requirements.spec: Add src/scenes/FriendsScene.js (scene key 'Friends'), registered in main.js and reached from a 'Friends' button on the menu. One card per friend the player has met (a guest in a level they have opened): portrait, name, and their permanent needs from rules.json characters. A need is shown ONLY after the player has cleared (1+ stars) a level where that friend is a guest and the chat has a line tagged with that need; until then it shows '???'. Never reveal a need earlier: that would solve implied clues. Friends not met yet show only '???'.

requirements.title: Game and tools use the new assets/ folders
requirements.bible: Game identity > Audio and Art: music is hand-picked by Gabriella and credited; art comes from her source images. Gabriella moved art/source/ to assets/art/ and the music to assets/music/ (2026-11-13).
requirements.spec: Source art now lives in assets/art/ and music in assets/music/ (both at the repo root, one level above game/). 1) tools/slice_portraits.py: read from assets/art (SRC = os.path.join(ROOT, 'assets', 'art')) and update its docstrings. 2) Add tools/sync_assets.mjs (Node, no dependencies): copy every .mp3/.ogg and *-license.txt from ../assets/music/ into public/music/ (create the folder; remove files there that are no longer in assets/music/); print what it copied. 3) package.json scripts: "sync-assets": "node tools/sync_assets.mjs", plus "predev", "prebuild" and "preboot-test" that run it, so the music is always in place for the dev server, builds and tests. 4) Change every remaining 'art/source' mention in src/ and CLAUDE.md to 'assets/art' (e.g. the Outcome image placeholder text, comments in theme.js and cityMap.js, the Art section of CLAUDE.md), and say in CLAUDE.md that game/public/music/ is a generated copy of assets/music/ (ignored by Git). Never move, rename or delete files in assets/.

requirements.title: Speaker icon has a slash through it, in the icon's border colour, when muted or at volume 0
requirements.bible: The music volume control on every screen (Gabriella, 2026-11-13).
requirements.spec: In src/scenes/HudScene.js, when music is off OR the volume is 0, draw the speaker button with a bold diagonal slash right across the whole round button (from its top-left edge to its bottom-right edge, about 3 px wide, in the same colour as the button's border ring (C.label, read when drawing so High contrast applies), over the speaker shape), and no sound waves. Put it in a function drawMutedSlash(g) that draw() calls. When music is on and the volume is above 0, no slash. The slash must update as soon as the slider reaches 0 or the On/Off switch is used.

requirements.title: Chapter intro card before How to play
requirements.bible: Campaign structure > Calendar (chapter seasons). Gabriella, 2026-11-13: the chapter 1 card comes before How to play.
requirements.spec: Add src/logic/introOrder.js (pure, no Phaser) exporting introSteps(levelNumber, seen) where seen = { howToPlay: bool, chapter: bool }, returning the ordered list of intros to show before the chat starts: the chapter card first (when not seen), then How to play (only for level 1, when not seen). So a first visit to level 1 gives ['chapter', 'howToPlay']. ChatScene.startWithIntros() must follow introSteps(): show each in turn, then start the chat. Keep the first 2 messages showing behind How to play (FIRST_TIME_LINES); the chapter card can show over the empty chat. Add a check of introSteps to test/boot-test.mjs (first visit to level 1 -> ['chapter','howToPlay']; level 2 with nothing seen -> []; level 6 with the chapter unseen -> ['chapter']).

requirements.title: New friend cards: one line about each friend; Liam then Cyrus in level 1
requirements.bible: Cast: permanent constraints (Cyrus peanut allergy, Mina vegetarian, Brooke health conscious, Maya budget, Roxy dairy intolerance; Liam none, always hungry). Clue rules: implied clues are never said outright before the player has solved them.
requirements.spec: Add src/logic/friendTaglines.js exporting FRIEND_TAGLINES = { cyrus: 'peanut allergy', mina: 'vegetarian', brooke: 'healthy foods', maya: 'on a budget', roxy: 'dairy intolerance', liam: 'always hungry, down for anything' } (Gabriella gave Cyrus, Mina and Brooke; the other three follow the bible's Cast and she may reword them). On the Outcome screen's 'A new friend has joined!' card, show the friend's tagline under their name instead of 'say hi on your Friends page'. Because the tagline names a need, welcome a friend only on a level the player CLEARS (1+ stars), never after a fail (a fail would hand the answer to the retry): src/ui/friendsAnnounced.js stays the record. Order and flow: in level 1 the first card is Liam; clicking 'Next friend →' (or clicking anywhere on the card outside its buttons) shows Cyrus's card; the last card's button says 'Keep going'.

requirements.title: Volume panel closes when you click outside it
requirements.bible: The music volume control on every screen (Gabriella, 2026-11-13): hide the volume slider when the area outside its box is clicked.
requirements.spec: In src/scenes/HudScene.js, the open volume panel closes on any click or tap outside the panel box (PANEL) and the speaker button: anywhere on any screen, including on other screens' buttons and cards, AND anywhere in the browser page outside the game canvas (the dark bars around the game when the window is not the game's shape): add a window-level pointerdown listener (window.addEventListener('pointerdown', ...)) that closes the panel when the click is outside the canvas, and remove it when the Hud shuts down. Put the check in a function closeIfOutside(...). Clicks inside the panel box (the slider, the On/Off switch, or the panel background) keep it open. Esc also closes it (keydown-ESC), without stopping the screen underneath from using Esc for its own back action. Keep M as the toggle.

requirements.title: Esc closes the volume panel and nothing else
requirements.bible: The music volume control on every screen (Gabriella, 2026-11-13): allow pressing Esc to close the volume slider.
requirements.spec: While the volume panel is open, pressing Esc closes the panel and does nothing else: the screen underneath (Options, Credits, Friends, Scrapbook, Chat, Results, Outcome and so on) must not also act on that same Esc press (no 'back' to the menu, no closing of that screen's own cards). With the panel closed, Esc works on each screen exactly as before. Do it in src/scenes/HudScene.js: the Hud is the top scene, so in its keydown-ESC handler, when the panel is open, close it and call event.stopImmediatePropagation() on the keyboard event so lower scenes don't receive it; also set this.registry 'hudPanelOpen' while the panel is open and clear it when it closes, so any screen whose Esc handler still fires can ignore Esc while it's set (add that check to the Esc handlers in OptionsScene, CreditsScene, FriendsScene and ScrapbookScene).

requirements.title: Title screen with the title_screen_v1 picture and the title over it
requirements.bible: Title screen (Gabriella, 2026-11-22): use the title_screen_v1 image; put the Let's Eat title and catch phrase on top of it.
requirements.spec: Add a title screen shown once after Boot and before the level map (Menu). Art: the picked draft title_screen_v1.jpg (1375x768, from the art worktree's assets/drafts/gemini/title_screen/) is copied to assets/art/title_screen.jpg; tools/slice_portraits.py copies it unchanged to public/art-preview/ui/title_screen.jpg and adds it to the manifest's 'ui' group under the key 'title_screen'. New src/scenes/TitleScene.js (scene key 'Title', registered in src/main.js; BootScene starts 'Title' instead of 'Menu'): draw the picture filling the 960x640 screen without stretching (scale to cover, crop the sides evenly). Over it, near the top where the sky is, draw the title "LET'S EAT!" and the catch phrase 'read the chat · f‌ind the spot · feed your friends' (same fonts and colours as the Menu's old title) on a dark translucent fade or plate so they stay readable. Keep the friends' faces in the lower half clear. A 'Start' button (and Enter, Space or a click anywhere) goes to Menu. If the texture is missing, draw the title on the plain background instead. Dev shortcuts that open a scene directly (?scene=...) skip the title screen.

requirements.title: No title or catch phrase on the level map screen
requirements.bible: Title screen (Gabriella, 2026-11-22): remove the title and catch phrase from the level/map screen; they live on the title screen now.
requirements.spec: The level map screen (src/scenes/MenuScene.js) shows no "LET'S EAT!" title and no catch phrase. Remove the drawn title and catch-phrase text (the fallback used when there is no City Map art). Note: the City Map picture (assets/art/City Map.jpg) has 'LET'S EAT / FEED YOUR FRIENDS' painted into its top centre (about x 450-950, y 15-110 of 1408x768), so removing the code text alone does not hide it. Gabriella supplies a title-free City Map; until then the code must not add the title back, and the requirement is only fully met once the map art no longer shows it.

requirements.title: Level map: back button, Esc and Backspace return to the title screen
requirements.bible: Level map screen (Gabriella, 2026-11-23): add a back button players can click to go to the title page; pressing Esc or Back also returns to the title page.
requirements.spec: In src/scenes/MenuScene.js (the level/city map screen) add a '← Title' button in the top-left corner, styled like the '← Levels' back buttons on the other screens (button(..., { w: 120, h: 34, size: 15, fill: C.bar })), that starts the 'Title' scene. Move the Options and Credits buttons down so the three stack without overlapping each other or the map's district hotspots. Pressing Esc (keydown-ESC) or Backspace (keydown-BACKSPACE) on the map also starts 'Title'; ignore them while the volume panel is open (this.registry.get('hudPanelOpen')), like the other screens' Esc handlers. Keyboard play on the map (arrows, Enter, O, C, F) keeps working as before.

requirements.title: Credits as a see-through overlay on the title screen picture
requirements.bible: Credits screen (Gabriella, 2026-11-23): make the credits page a transparent overlay, with the title page image as the background.
requirements.spec: In src/scenes/CreditsScene.js draw the title screen picture (texture key 'title_screen', the same one TitleScene uses) filling the 960x640 screen without stretching (scale to cover, crop evenly), then a dark see-through layer over it so text stays readable, and make the credits panel translucent (about 80-85% opaque) so the picture shows through around and behind it. The header (title, subtitle, '← Levels' button) sits over the picture with a dark fade or shadow so it reads. Keep everything else: the slow roll, scrolling, Esc back. If the texture is missing, keep today's plain background.

requirements.title: Options: a toggle to turn off the page animations (Scrapbook, Friends)
requirements.bible: Options (Gabriella, 2026-11-23): add a toggle to turn off animations on the Scrapbook and Friends pages.
requirements.spec: Add a setting 'pageAnimations' to src/ui/settings.js with two options, On (default) and Off, saved like the other settings, and export a helper pageAnimations() that returns true when it is On and Reduce motion is off. Add a row to src/scenes/OptionsScene.js: title 'Page animations', about 'Page turns in the Scrapbook and on the Friends page, and the badge being stuck on.' Six rows must still fit above the key hint at the bottom (shrink ROW_H or the row spacing as needed) and keyboard focus must still reach every row. When pageAnimations() is false: on the Friends page (src/scenes/FriendsScene.js) switching friends changes the page at once, with no page turn; in the Scrapbook (src/scenes/ScrapbookScene.js) switching pages changes the spread at once, with no page turn, and the rosette badge simply appears, with no drop, squash, ring or sparkles. Everything else on those screens (tabs, clicks, arrow keys) works the same. (2026-11-23, Gabriella: the separate Options row was later folded into the single 'Animations' toggle; see animations_one_toggle.)

requirements.title: Title screen: Start always works, also after coming back from the map
requirements.bible: Title screen (Gabriella, 2026-11-23): after going back to the title from the level map ('← Title' or Backspace), the Start button stops working. Start must always go to the level map.
requirements.spec: Bug: src/scenes/TitleScene.js go() sets this.leaving = true and never clears it. Phaser reuses the scene object, so the second time the title screen is shown, go() returns straight away and Start, Enter, Space and clicks do nothing. Fix: reset this.leaving = false at the start of create(). Also add a check to test/browser-boot.mjs that boots the game, goes Title -> Menu (Enter), back to Title (Backspace), then presses Enter again and confirms the Menu scene is active.

requirements.title: Backspace returns to the level map from Options, Scrapbook and Friends
requirements.bible: Controls (Gabriella, 2026-11-23): allow Backspace on the Options, Scrapbook and Friends screens to return to the level screen.
requirements.spec: In src/scenes/OptionsScene.js, src/scenes/ScrapbookScene.js and src/scenes/FriendsScene.js, pressing Backspace (keydown-BACKSPACE) does the same as Esc there: go back to the level map ('Menu'). Ignore it while the volume panel is open (this.registry.get('hudPanelOpen')), like Esc. Esc keeps working as before.

requirements.title: Credits: the panel a little more see-through
requirements.bible: Credits screen (Gabriella, 2026-11-23): make the white credits panel slightly more transparent.
requirements.spec: In src/scenes/CreditsScene.js lower PANEL_ALPHA from 0.84 to 0.70, so more of the title picture shows through the credits panel. The credit text must stay easy to read: if it no longer is, darken the see-through layer over the picture slightly rather than raising the panel's alpha again.

requirements.title: Options: 'Reduce motion' becomes 'Animations', with a live preview
requirements.bible: Options (Gabriella, 2026-11-23): reword 'Reduce motion' as 'Animations' and add a preview of the animation.
requirements.spec: In src/scenes/OptionsScene.js rename the 'Reduce motion' row to 'Animations', with the meaning flipped so On means animations play: in src/ui/settings.js the motion options become [{ id: 'reduced', label: 'Off' }, { id: 'full', label: 'On' }] (same stored ids, so saved settings keep working; Off/On order like the other rows). About text: 'Sliding, popping, pulsing and spinning. Off: things simply appear.' Add a method previewMotion() that animates the Options PREVIEW panel when Animations is On: the preview's three stars pop in one after another (scale 0 to 1, Back.easeOut, like the Outcome screen) and the chat bubble slides in, repeating every 2-3 seconds. When Animations is Off, the preview is shown still, all at once. Changing the setting updates the preview straight away (the screen already redraws on change). Keep the 'Page animations' row; its about text should still make sense next to the renamed row.

requirements.title: Backspace returns to the level map from Credits
requirements.bible: Controls (Gabriella, 2026-11-23): allow Backspace on the Credits screen to return to the level screen.
requirements.spec: In src/scenes/CreditsScene.js, pressing Backspace (keydown-BACKSPACE) does the same as Esc: go back to the level map ('Menu'). Ignore it while the volume panel is open (this.registry.get('hudPanelOpen')), like Esc. Esc and the scrolling keys keep working as before.

requirements.title: Credits: the panel even more see-through
requirements.bible: Credits screen (Gabriella, 2026-11-23): make the white credits panel even more transparent (after it went from 84% to 70%).
requirements.spec: In src/scenes/CreditsScene.js lower PANEL_ALPHA from 0.70 to 0.55, so more of the title picture shows through. The credit text must stay easy to read: if it no longer is, darken the see-through layer over the picture (or give the text a soft light outline) rather than raising the panel's alpha again.

requirements.title: Options: one 'Animations' toggle for everything, page turns included

The 'Animations' row now covers everything; about text: 'Sliding, popping, page turns and the badge sticking on. Off: things simply appear.' requirements.title: Credits: no light outline around the words
requirements.bible: Credits screen (Gabriella, 2026-11-23): remove the white outline around the words.
requirements.spec: In src/scenes/CreditsScene.js remove the soft light outline on the credit text: drop TEXT_HALO_PX and the setStroke(...) call on the panel's text objects, so the words are drawn plain. requirements.title: Back buttons ('← Title', '← Levels') the same size as Options and Credits
requirements.bible: Buttons (Gabriella, 2026-11-23): make the '← Title' and '← Levels' buttons the same dimensions as the Options and Credits buttons.

requirements.title: The map's Friends button in Mina's orange

requirements.title: Chat: Backspace goes back to the level map
requirements.bible: Controls (Gabriella, 2026-11-23): on the chat screen, Backspace returns to the levels.
requirements.spec: In src/scenes/ChatScene.js pressing Backspace (keydown-BACKSPACE) does what the '← Levels' button does: this.scene.start('Menu'). requirements.title: Unlock cards: the focus ring appears only once the buttons are shown
requirements.bible: Outcome screen (Gabriella, 2026-11-23): when a new Scrapbook page is unlocked, show the highlight around the button only once 'Keep going' is visible; during the animation the button isn't visible yet but its highlight already is.
requirements.spec: In src/scenes/OutcomeScene.js showNextUnlock() calls drawFocus() straight away, so the focus ring is drawn around 'Keep going' / 'Next →' about a second before the buttons fade in (delay 950 ms). Fix, for both kinds of unlock card (new Scrapbook page, new friend): add unlockCard.ready = false when the card is made; while it is false, activeButtons() returns no buttons (so no ring is drawn and Enter/arrow keys do nothing on the card); set it true in the onComplete of the buttons' fade-in tween and call drawFocus() then. With Reduce motion / Animations off the tween completes at once, so the ring shows straight away. A click on the card or Esc still moves on as before.

requirements.spec: src/scenes/EndingScene.js (scene key 'Ending'), one scene in two parts, matching the drafts on the Art Artifacts 'Ending' tab (assets/drafts/screens/ending/ on master: v2 then v1). PART 1, THE FINAL GROUP CHAT: the Chat screen's look (chapter 4 backdrop chat_bg_chapter_04, portraits, names, white bubbles, typing bubbles at the Chat pace setting), headed 'THE GROUP CHAT' with 'the next morning'. Maya's first message carries a photo inside her bubble (art ending_coast_photo); everyone reacts; the last message thanks the player. When every line is shown, a 'The End' card on the right shows the campaign stars (earned / max), the six friends' faces and a Continue button (Enter / → also continue). The chat scrolls when it overflows. PART 2, THE GROUP PHOTO + ROLL CALL: an open book like the Scrapbook, titled 'THE SEND-OFF' / 'chapter 4 · waterfront · the end'. Left page: a polaroid of all six at the send-off table (art ending_group_photo) dropped and taped on, with a handwritten caption. Right page: 'ROLL CALL', one closing line per friend with their portrait and name colour, appearing one by one. Then 'thanks for always knowing where to eat.' and Continue, which returns to the map. LINES: from content/campaign/ending.json, bundled like the level files in src/content.js (an optional import.meta.glob, so a missing file is not an error). Schema: { "chat": [{ "speaker", "emotion", "text", "photo"?: true }], "roll_call": { "<friend id>": { "text", "emotion" } }, "caption", "generated_by", "edited_by" }. The game never writes these lines itself: until the narrative writer has written the file, show grey placeholder bubbles/rows reading '[line to come]' so the layout can be tested. ART: ending_coast_photo and ending_group_photo through the asset manifest like other art; until they exist, the striped 'ART GOES HERE' placeholder naming the file (as the Scrapbook does). WHEN: it plays once, after Continue on the level_20 Outcome screen when the pick was perfect; a flag in localStorage ('lets-eat-ending-seen-v1') stops it repeating, and Reset progress clears it. Esc / Backspace skip to part 2, then to the map. Dev shortcut: ?scene=Ending. Animations follow the Animations option (off: things simply appear). Sounds through src/ui/sfx.js: outcome_perfect as the polaroid lands, badge_stuck for the tape, click on Continue. Keep the bottom-left 44 px free for the music button. Register the scene in src/main.js, add it to the browser boot test, and add an 'Ending' bullet to game/CLAUDE.md.
